operationalSituations.description: pyfusa check/trace/qualify run in CI against a Python project's source tree
pyfusa fmea/tara/hara/safety-case/sas/sci run to generate evidence artifacts consumed by a certification review

hazards.description: False negative — the tool fails to detect a safety-critical coding violation it claims to cover
False positive — the tool reports a violation that does not actually exist, eroding trust until users disable the tool entirely
Non-deterministic fingerprint — the same finding produces different fingerprints across runs, breaking disposition matching and diff
Incorrect exit code — a gate failure (open ERROR finding) is not reported as exit 1, so a CI pipeline proceeds past a real defect

safetyGoals.description: The tool shall detect all MUST-check rules listed in the x-FuSa spec §9.1 with no systematic omission
safetyGoals.safeState: N/A — analysis-time tool, not a controlling system; the safe state is a complete, versioned rule registry with test coverage per rule

safetyGoals.description: An unwanted finding shall be dispositionable (accept/defer) rather than requiring the tool to be disabled outright
safetyGoals.safeState: N/A — the disposition mechanism itself is the mitigation

safetyGoals.description: The fingerprint algorithm shall be deterministic per §4.2 for identical (ruleId, file, message) input
safetyGoals.safeState: N/A — determinism is a pure-function correctness property, verified by test

safetyGoals.description: Exit codes shall conform to §2.3 in all circumstances (0/1/2/3 per the documented semantics)
safetyGoals.safeState: N/A — exit-code correctness is verified by test across every command
